summary: Xbox Game Pass Ultimate offers robust access to Microsoft's game library, including first-party titles and online multiplayer access on both console and PC via the Xbox app. Although monthly costs have been reduced from $29.99 to $22.99, readers can secure a better deal by purchasing a three-month subscription digital code for $39.01 (valued at $69). This discount allows gamers to access services like playing *Halo: Campaign Evolved* when it launches July 28th on Xbox and PC, offering substantial savings over buying games outright.
author: Cameron Faulkner
content: Subscribing to Xbox Game Pass Ultimate on a recurring basis has been tough to justify recently, even after Microsoft reduced the monthly cost from $29.99 to $22.99. But you can get a better deal on a three-month subscription (valued at $69) by grabbing a digital code at Eneba that costs $39.01 at the time of publication. Game Pass Ultimate grants you access to the full Game Pass library on Xbox (compared to a more limited slice with Premium), including first-party titles and online multiplayer access. The subscription also gives PC gamers access to Microsoft's catalog of Game Pass games through the Xbox app, though the selection differs a bit between console and desktop. You don't need me to tell you why deals like these are nice. The costs of subscriptions generally only go in one direction over time, and it is becoming more rare to find worthwhile discounts that give you a break. If you want to jump into Halo: Campaign Evolved when it launches July 28th on Xbox and PC, all you need is this subscription instead of buying the $49.99 re-remake.

title: Carrie is just trying to make a friend in the new trailer
teaser: Mike Flanagan's 'Carrie' tackles modern teen trauma: social media bullying and active shooter drills debut Oct 7th on Amazon Prime.
summary: Mike Flanagan's fourth Stephen King adaptation, 'Carrie,' is slated for Amazon Prime on October 7th. The film updates the classic narrative to address modern issues such as social media bullying and active shooter drills. According to reports, Flanagan incorporated real-life traumas shared by high school students during the writing process, focusing on the nature of internet cruelty. While the franchise features the iconic 1976 version with Sissy Spacek, this adaptation utilizes Summer H. Howell, who is considered more believable in a modern student role.
author: Terrence O’Brien
content: Mike Flanagan's latest Stephen King adaptation, Carrie (this will be his fourth), is slated to make its debut on Amazon Prime on October 7th. The new trailer dropped at Comic-Con 2026 and doesn't contain many surprises. If you're familiar with Carrie at all, it hits all the expected notes. Though it's clearly been updated for the modern era. According to Deadline , Flanagan's take on the classic King novel will tackle very modern teen challenges like active shooter drills and bullying on social media. The director apparently invited high schoolers into the writers' room, using their real-life traumas to inform the script: "They shared shocking one-off situations or constant treatment and microaggressions and things that are not necessarily present themselves as targeted harassment. [We will dive into] the cruelty in today's world and how the internet has encouraged cruelty, rewards and celebrates and amplifies it. This is awful for adults to deal with, and for teenagers even more so." Brian De Palma's iconic 1976 adaptation of Carrie is iconic and features an unimpeachable performance from Sissy Spacek. But it's undeniable that Summer H. Howell, who was 21 at the time of shooting, is much more believable as a high school student than Spacek, who was 26 at the time.

title: Champagne and Bullets belongs on the Mount Rushmore of bad movies
teaser: This wild cinematic curiosity features an entire plot involving cults, sex scenes set to songs, and inexplicably bad relationships.
summary: This article reviews the cult film "Champagne and Bullets," an example of a 'so bad they're good' movie. The entire production was by John De Hart, who wrote, directed, and starred as Rick Bode. The plot follows cops Bode and Finney after losing their badges, leading to extreme events like prison-related cult formation and the reappearance of ex-girlfriend Cindy, who is fleeing a satanic coven. Reviewers highlight the film's overabundance of awkward material, including three lengthy sex scenes with Pamela Bryant (totaling 12 minutes) set to songs sung by Hart, which contrasts sharply with the scant action and inexplicable character interactions. The movie can be found on Hoopla, Amazon Prime, and Tubi.
author: Terrence O’Brien
content: There's something about a movie like The Room , Troll 2 , or Fateful Findings that I find irresistible. These sorts of "so bad they're good" films are marvelous curiosities where ambition far outstrips resources, ability, and self-awareness to become something much greater than the sum of their parts. Champagne and Bullets (also released as GetEven and Road to Revenge ) is a film on par with those classics of outsider cinema. The movie is almost entirely the work of one man, John De Hart. Hart wrote, directed, and stars as Rick Bode in the film. He even performs a musical number early in the proceedings - The bizarre " Shimmy Slide ." During the performance, Hart, who was reportedly pumped full of painkillers after throwing out his back, is stiff and looks around the room as if he's only performing under threat of violence. And somehow, this lifeless performance of a cringy country rocker isn't the most awkward scene in the movie. The relationships and interactions between characters in Champagne and Bullets are just as inexplicable and unnatural as those in The Room . Bode and his partner Huck Finney are cops who lose their badges five minutes into the movie. This precipitates the alarmingly quick mental decline of Finney, who is also going through a divorce after discovering his wife has been sleeping around. He fires a handgun through his bills, drinks bleach to get out of prison, and seemingly starts a cult. Oh, and speaking of cults, a good portion of the plot revolves around the reemergence of Bode's old girlfriend Cindy, who is fleeing a satanic coven that "sacrificed a human baby." While ostensibly an action film, the fight scenes are few and far between, and staged with all the believability of a theme park stunt show. Hart seemed far more interested in cramming in as much gratuitous nudity as possible. There are three uncomfortably long sex scenes with costar Pamela Bryant, who plays Cindy, all set to songs sung by Hart. In total, they take up 12 minutes of runtime in a movie that is only 90 minutes long. One scene that takes place in a jacuzzi apparently even led Hart's girlfriend at the time to break up with him. (Warning: One scene not involving Hart and Bryant does depict a sexual assault.) If you're a fan of bad movies, cult classics, or the podcast How Did This Get Made , you owe it to yourself to go watch Champagne and Bullets. It's available on Hoopla , Amazon Prime , and Tubi .
